summary: Climate change has made rain and drought increasingly unpredictable, and farmers bear the cost with every planting decision. GoFarm turns that uncertainty into clear guidance. From a farm’s location, three specialized AI agents work together. The Climate Agent analyzes temperature, rainfall, and solar radiation using NASA POWER data. The Soil Agent evaluates soil properties, organic matter, and erosion risk with USDA SSURGO. The Market Agent studies years of crop prices and yields from USDA NASS QuickStats. Finally, a Judge Agent weighs their verdicts according to the farmer’s priority (protecting the soil, saving water, or a balanced approach) and delivers one clear recommendation. GoFarm gives farmers confidence not only in their land and climate, but also in their market, helping them plant smarter, use resources wisely, and adapt to a changing world.
details:
FarmGo is a tool that works with an artificial intelligence ecosystem to help farmers decide what to plant in a changing climate. The farmer selects a location on an interactive map, and the system sends that point’s data to a team of specialized agents: a Climate Agent working with NASA POWER, a Soil Agent working with USDA SSURGO, and a Market Agent working with USDA NASS QuickStats. Rather than simply listing results, the agents debate their findings with real data, and a Judge Agent weighs that discussion according to what the farmer cares about most, whether saving water, protecting the soil, or a balanced approach, before delivering a final recommendation. An integrated chatbot, connected to NASA POWER climate data and market data, stays available to answer any question about the farmer’s crops. Because it also draws on the agents’ discussion, it can explain soil-related questions too. This is where the innovation lies: not in using AI agents, but in assembling them so they challenge one another, which gives farmers confidence in their land, their climate, and their market at once. Our friendly mascot, Blueby, makes that experience approachable.

We built the frontend with Next.js and the backend in Python with FastAPI, using GPT-OSS 20B, GPT-OSS 120B, and Qwen through the Groq API. We chose these models for their strong tool-calling abilities, and Qwen in particular for delivering high performance at a lighter size. Because this is an MVP, we focused on Texas and a selected set of crops, since it is one of the U.S. states most affected by drought and climate variability. The architecture is designed to scale, so the same approach can eventually support farms anywhere in the world. Our intended impact is for farmers to plant smarter, use water wisely, and adapt to a changing climate with clear, trustworthy guidance.
